title: Das Übliche?
desc: Somebody starts your coffee before you get there
setting: Quarter past seven, the machine already running, and a question that is not really a question.

options.feedback: Two words, and the second one carries all of it. Gern is how enthusiasm is said here.
You gave her the word back. That is exactly what a regular does with it.
Fair, the first time. But she has watched you order the same thing forty mornings running.
Three words and it is true. She has heard it from everybody who arrives, and she asks anyway.
Correct and closed. One sentence more is what turns this into a conversation.
A closed door. Ja on its own ends it, and she was opening something.
You do. And agreeing with a small direct observation is the whole answer here.

options.en: I do not have much time.
options.feedback: True, and she will point out that the coffee costs the same sitting down.
She has watched you do it for a month. This is a correction and it is meant kindly.
You said it back. Ade is for a guest, bis morgen is for somebody who is coming back.
Not wrong, and it is the more distant of the two. She just gave you the closer one.
You will be there at quarter past seven and both of you know it.
